analysis: This batch contains only documentation: a new changelog fragment (changelog.d/deadline-admission-estimators.md, lines 1-6) and a new 'Deadline admission rates' section in docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (head lines 457-482) plus one code-map row (head line 536). No executable code is in the supplied units. The docs describe provider-local changes to first-token deadline admission estimators: per-step decode pricing, MTP depth capped by the automatic verification envelope, an anchor and one-eighth floor for isolated-prefill rate, 30-minute evidence staleness, and a DARKBLOOM_TTFT_ADMISSION_FIXES=0 rollback env var forwarded by `darkbloom start`. Docs state no change to KV grants, load quotation, activation floor, serving width or memory admission, and that published rates and capacity wire fields are unchanged. Threat-model relevance is limited: the deadline admission is an availability and scheduling time check, not an authentication, encryption or attestation control. No change touches T-008 plaintext fail-closed, TB-002 wire contract, App Attest authorization (TB-011) or prefix-cache storage (T-041). Possible availability considerations include an operator-influenced calibration, a lower pricing floor admitting more work (T-010/T-029 adjacent), and the new env var as an operator-local rollback switch (ADV-001 already controls the provider). All of these are unverified because the actual implementation (AdmissionRateEstimators.swift, EngineV2Bridge+Admission.swift, StartCommand env forwarding) is not supplied. The next pass should check that env forwarding in launchd plist generation does not widen env injection, and that the 1/8 floor and idle-expiry logic cannot admit requests beyond the slot/process byte admission. These are code-review questions, not findings from this evidence.
